newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Kosovo Albanians want to join Yugo bank system.
newsitem.headline: Kosovo Albanians want to join Yugo bank system.

text.p: A group of ethnic Albanian bankers have proposed Serbia revitalise Kosovska Banka which has been under receivership since December 1990, the daily Danas reported on Thursday.
Revitalisation of Kosovska could also clear the path to resolving some other problems in Serbia's mostly-Albanian southern province of Kosovo, the paper said.
Albanians wanted a revitalised Kosovska to join the Yugoslav banking system in which the region accounted for only two percent of total bank deposits and two percent of total dinar loans, Danas said.

"Revitalisation of the bank would be a part of wider democratisation, privatisation and liberalisation of Serbia's economy and Kosovska should become an important, independent financial institution for the Kosovo economy," Danas quoted ex-head of Kosovska, Ilijaz Ilijazi, as saying.

"Political leadership will realise that revitalisation of Kosovska can bring only positive economic effects and indirectly positive political effects for the entire situation in Kosovo," Ilijazi said.
Banks operating in Kosovo, affiliates of banks based outside the province and without licences for international payment and credit operations, have been blamed for moving capital from the region.
Ethnic Albanian bankers saw a revitalised Kosovska as a way to attract expatriate capital, pensions, and savings.
A financially strengthened Kosovska would also help revamp Kosovo's ailing and backward economy, Ilijazi said.

Ilijazi insisted the region needed to establish an adequate financial infrastructure, including a bourse, brokerages and other financial institutions to make the system compatible with that of Yugoslavia and the outside world.
